title: The agent writes the next notebook cell for the person's request; an accepted cell runs in the kernel
request: I asked show accuracy plot but nothing happened; again I asked show accuracy plot, nothing when I clicked Accept; the sample notebook must connect to the real project; fix all bugs in this area.
spec: The owner's bug-finder rules for the hunt: high-severity only, a concrete trigger for each, a minimal fix and a test.
plan: A notebook_cell purpose and prompt: the request, the notebook's code cells and the column names with kinds, never a row
Check every proposal before it is shown: it parses, it never touches X_test or y_test; one retry told what failed
Routes to write, accept or reject; an accepted cell runs by its id after the check again
The page: real proposals with Accept and Reject, Run with outputs and plots; the Notebook page opens the latest real project
A bug hunt over the area with the reviewer, then fix every finding with a test

decisions.decision: Only an accepted cell runs, and it is checked again right before it runs.
decisions.why: The person decides what code runs; a stored cell changed after the answer is refused.

decisions.decision: The Notebook page opens the latest real project, its solution saved first, whatever sample was chosen elsewhere.
decisions.why: The owner: the sample notebook must connect to the real project; the sample shows only when no project exists.

decisions.decision: The server runs the notebook's cells up to the holdout before an agent's cell on a kernel that has run nothing.
decisions.why: The page cannot know when the server swept, restarted or replaced the kernel.

decisions.decision: Who may run agent cells stays the owner's choice (any signed-in member) and is reported as the open risk.
decisions.why: The owner chose it knowingly; the sandbox step in the roadmap is the real boundary, a role check is not one for a friend who owns a workspace.

change: studio/notebook_agent.py (new), prompts/notebook_cell.md (new), models/settings.py (notebook_cell), agents/harness.py, studio/kernels.py, expansion/datasets.py (row_order), studio/engine.py, routers/projects.py (write, answer, run by id, review fields), accounts/guard.py, the Notebook page, tests.

findings.defect: Ask the agent to write the next cell did nothing real.
findings.scenario: The person asked for an accuracy plot on the Notebook page; a fixed example cell appeared, and Accept only showed a message.
findings.cause: The box was the demo's: a written example in sample mode and hidden on a real project.
findings.fix: A model writes the cell from the notebook and the columns; Accept and Run work on a real project; the sample says it is a sample.

findings.defect: A time split put the holdout rows into the kernel.
findings.scenario: A table with its newest rows first and a time column: the kernel's table held the latest rows, which the holdout scores.
findings.cause: The time split sorts the rows by time and counts its train rows in that order; the row positions kept the file's order.
findings.fix: The bundle keeps its row order and the engine maps the positions through it; a table of other rows (entities) is refused.

findings.defect: A live kernel kept the old training rows after the solution changed.
findings.scenario: Cells run on a random split, then a time column is saved: the kernel still read the old rows, most of the new holdout among them.
findings.cause: A live kernel was reused whatever the table, solution or settings were now.
findings.fix: Each kernel keeps a fingerprint of the table, the solution and the settings; a different one restarts it with the new rows.

findings.defect: A restart during a run spun the processor and ended in a server error.
findings.scenario: Restart pressed while a long cell ran: the run looped on a closed channel until its timeout, then the interrupt raised.
findings.cause: Every exception while waiting for a message was taken as no message yet; the interrupt was not guarded.
findings.fix: Only an empty queue waits again, and only while the kernel lives; a stopped kernel ends the run with its reason.

findings.defect: Two overlapping requests lost an answer or a proposal.
findings.scenario: The person accepted a cell while another was being written: the write saved the list it read before, so the cell showed accepted and Run refused it.
findings.cause: Both routes read the list, waited, and wrote the whole list back.
findings.fix: A lock per project around reading and writing the list, read again right before the write.

findings.defect: An agent's cell failed with a missing name on a kernel the page did not start.
findings.scenario: After the idle sweep or a restart by someone else, Run again on an accepted cell: X_train was not defined.
findings.cause: The page decided whether the kernel was new from its own memory.
findings.fix: The server runs the notebook's cells first on a kernel that has run nothing and says how many.

findings.defect: Code runs were cut before they were saved.
findings.scenario: A cell printing a long text or a long traceback: the record kept only the cut text and counted the pictures.
findings.cause: The text was cut where the outputs were collected, before the record.
findings.fix: The record keeps every output whole with its pictures; only the page's copy is cut.

findings.defect: Accepted cells could be dropped from the kept list.
findings.scenario: Many refused writes pushed the oldest cells out, an accepted one among them.
findings.cause: The list was cut to its last entries whatever their state.
findings.fix: Refused and rejected cells go first, then old proposals; an accepted cell stays.

findings.defect: My code edits reloaded the owner's development server while the owner was using the page.
findings.scenario: Edits to the package one by one restarted the server and its kernel in the middle of the owner's try.
findings.cause: make dev reloads on every change under dclab_rnd.
findings.fix: Batch the edits to the package and tell the owner before and after; the owner's cell stayed proposed for them to accept.

measurements.name: Live cell for show accuracy plot
measurements.gate: the cell parses, never reads the holdout, runs and draws a plot
measurements.result: Sonnet wrote a fold-accuracy plot with a majority-class baseline from the training folds; it ran and returned a picture; 1,963 input and 508 output tokens
limits: one request on a sample table; accuracy equals the majority-class baseline there, so the plot says little about the model

measurements.name: The owner's project in the browser
measurements.gate: write, accept and run on a real project draw the plot
measurements.result: the cell for show accuracy plot was accepted and ran on the owner's project; the plot showed accuracy per time-ordered fold against the baseline

outcome: The agent writes the cell the person asks for on a real project, it is checked, accepted and run, and the time split, a changed solution, a restart and overlapping requests no longer break it.
lessons: A demo control that looks real must say it is a sample when clicked, or the person thinks the product is broken.
Row positions must follow every reordering of the rows, or the training rows the kernel gets are not the training rows.
risks: Any signed-in member can run code as the server's user until the sandbox step: they can read files the server can read.
